title: Entropy-driven exposure scheduler with early-stop and safety horizon
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and deliver a new exposure scheduler that adapts per-tenant traffic allocation during model A/B and canary rollouts driven by an entropy-based signal, with sequential early-stop checks and a safety horizon to automatically throttle or rollback variants that show unpredictable behavior. The goal is to reduce user-facing regressions while minimizing sample size and time-to-confidence for safe rollouts.
background: Current rollout tooling uses fixed exposure ramps and simple metric thresholds. We observed two recurring failure modes: (1) low-signal regressions that only appear in distributional changes (higher token-level entropy / hallucination patterns) and (2) late-detected degradations that require big rollbacks after large exposure. This ticket proposes an exposure controller that uses model-output entropy + composite quality signals to dynamically shape exposure and run sequential hypothesis tests with alpha-spending to decide early-stop or graceful throttling.
goals: Implement entropy as a first-class experiment signal (per-response and aggregate) and wire it into the rollout controller
Create an exposure scheduling algorithm that adapts allocation by signal strength while respecting tenant safety budgets
Add sequential statistical checks (alpha-spending, stopping boundaries) to allow early-stop with bounded false positive risk
Provide a safety horizon: conservative rollback policies when signal crosses critical thresholds, including automatic fallback to pinned model variant
Ship API + Console controls for experiment owners to tune safety budgets and view entropy-based diagnostics
acceptance_criteria: Entropy metric computed for all experiment responses and visible in per-route experiment dashboard
Scheduler can be configured per-experiment with initial allocation, max exposure, safety budget, and alpha parameters
Sequential checks trigger automatic throttles or rollback within configured SLO for false positive rate (alpha spending) during simulated tests
End-to-end tests that simulate distributional shift trigger early-stop in >95% of regression runs while keeping <5% false positive rate on controlled baselines
Docs and runbook published; two internal customers have pilot experiments using the scheduler
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Entropy is noisy at low token counts -> Mitigation: use smoothed rolling aggregates and per-session weighting
Risk: Over-eager early-stop may block valid upgrades -> Mitigation: alpha-spending + secondary human-in-the-loop override during pilot
Risk: Additional telemetry increases cost and latency -> Mitigation: sampling knobs and lightweight on-path computation with batched exports
Risk: Per-tenant tuning complexity -> Mitigation: sane defaults and a safety budget slider in Console
tradeoffs: We prioritize fast detection of distributional regressions at the cost of increased complexity and a new metric surface. There is a tradeoff between sensitivity (early detection) and specificity (false positives) managed via alpha spending and safety budgets. Initial rollout will focus on high-risk routes where customer impact is significant.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define entropy calculation and low-overhead on-path instrumentation (ENG infra work)
Phase 2: Scheduler algorithm + sequential test library implemented in rollout controller
Phase 4: Pilot with two internal customers and iterate on thresholds
Phase 5: GA and telemetry cost optimizations
test_plan: Unit tests for entropy computation and aggregation windows
Simulated A/B experiments with injected regressions to validate early-stop frequency and false positive rates
Load testing to ensure scheduler decisions do not add tail latency >5ms on 95th percentile
Chaos/incident drills for auto-rollback and human override paths
metrics: False positive rate of automatic rollback (should be <= configured alpha)
Customer error rate delta during pilot experiments
Average exposure per variant and safety budget consumption
notes: Initial DS spike (Marcus + Lina) validated that token-level entropy correlates with hallucination proxies on our public eval sets. We need ENG infra to expose per-request light histograms. Console UX will include a safety-horizon slider (5/10/25/50% budgets). Finance requests an estimate of monthly telemetry cost before GA.
